title: Helping a kids' brass band in Louisville
summary: He rehearsed a girls' welfare worker's children's brass band in Louisville and later met former pupils.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Did you ever do any teaching or help any pupils?

Well, yes, now in Louisville I did. I, uh, used to teach, uh, help the, help the band, uh, Miss, uh, was a lady. She was sort of a welfare worker and she had a, uh, little band. Got a band brass band together for kids. Uh-huh. And, uh, uh, his, uh, fellow, friend of mine, he started a band, Ralph Browne. And he left, uh, left Louisville. And so she came after me to come up and rehearse and help them. Yeah. And so I went up there and, uh, uh, worked with them for, for a good while and rehearsed them. And I saw some of those boys, uh, oh, I was with, I think it was with Earl. We were up in Pennsylvania. Oh, really? Around up in there and I'd seen several of those boys who were playing. And, uh, one of them was, uh, was with Fletcher Henderson. What was his name? He was a trombone player. Oh. Uh, oh, what was his name? Well, well. It wasn't Fields. You know, I can't think, can't think.

I was going to, uh, when you were taught, did you use a certain method, like a particular book that you liked better than others, or any? Or, well, now, uh, or you mean instruction books? Yes, when you teach them kids, I mean, start them on spagels and all.

No, no, well, they were playing when I went in there. Oh, I see, yeah. And, uh, uh, they had little, little books of marches and things. Oh, I see. Uh, uh, when I, when I was up there with them and I would just rehearse them, you know, rehearsing.
